title_en: China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd., Shanxi Branch v. Shanxi Shuozhou Pinglu District Hua Mei Ao Chong Sheng Coal Industry Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over loan contract
ruling_gist_en: In a guarantee contract for a maximum amount, if the contract explicitly stipulates that the maximum amount of the guaranteed claim includes the amount of the principal claim and the corresponding interest, liquidated damages, compensation for damages, and expenses for realizing the claim, the guarantor shall assume guarantee liability for the interest, liquidated damages, compensation for damages, and expenses for realizing the claim in accordance with the contract, and shall not be limited by the amount of the principal claim.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over loan contract; second instance trial; Supreme People's Court; Shanxi Province; Hebei Province; Guangdong Province; legal person; natural person; Guarantee Law; scope of guarantee for maximum amount; whether guarantee liability is limited by the amount of principal claim; bearing of expenses for realizing the claim; reversal of judgment; loan contract; maximum amount guarantee contract; interest, penalty interest, compound interest; attorney fees and preservation fees; contract dispute; security; guarantee; dispute over loan contract with an industry Co., Ltd., etc.
full_text_en:
China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd. Shanxi Branch v. 
Shanxi Shuozhou Pinglu District Hua Mei Ao Chong Sheng Coal Mining Co., Ltd. et al. 
— Dispute over loan contract

[Ruling Summary]

In a maximum guarantee contract relationship, if the contract expressly stipulates that the maximum amount of the secured claim includes the principal amount and the corresponding interest, liquidated damages, compensation for damages, and costs of realizing the claim, the guarantor shall assume the guarantee liability for such interest, liquidated damages, compensation for damages, and costs of realizing the claim in accordance with the contract, and shall not be limited by the amount of the principal claim.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) Supreme People's Court Final No. 823

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd. Shanxi Branch. Address: No. 16 Yingze West Street, Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province.
Responsible Person: Cao Zhiqiang, Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Xue Chao, Lawyer of Beijing Jingshi (Taiyuan) Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Wei Xiaohui, Lawyer of Beijing Jingshi (Taiyuan) Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Shanxi Shuozhou Pinglu District Hua Mei Ao Chong Sheng Coal Mining Co., Ltd. Address: Xiamiangao Village, Xiamiangao Township, Pinglu District, Shuozhou City, Shanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Ma Jihai, Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Zhou Zixiang, Legal Specialist of the Legal Department of the Company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Shanxi Hua Mei Ao Energy Group Co., Ltd. Address: Taocun Township, Pinglu District, Shuozhou City, Shanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Ma Jihai, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Jia Wenying, Employee of the Company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Zhuhai Qinfa Logistics Co., Ltd. Address: Room 551, Gaolan Customs Office Building, Zhuhai.
Legal Representative: Xu Da, Chairman of the Board of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Chen Yulan, Legal Supervisor of the Legal Department of the Company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Qinhuangdao Qinfa Industrial Group Co., Ltd. Address: No. 121 Yingbin Road, Haigang District, Qinhuangdao City, Hebei Province.
Legal Representative: Xu Da, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Shanxi Shuozhou Pinglu District Hua Mei Ao Fengxi Coal Mining Co., Ltd. Address: Fengjialing Village, Xiamiangao Township, Pinglu District, Shuozhou City, Shanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Wang Wenfu, Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Xie Huacong, Legal Specialist of the Legal Department of the Company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Xu Jihua, male, born on July 10, 1956, Han nationality, residing in Tongzhou District, Beijing.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Wang Guimin, female, born on November 30, 1959, Han nationality, residing in Haigang District, Qinhuangdao City, Hebei Province.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Xu Da, male, born on October 12, 1984, Han nationality, residing in Xuanwu District, Beijing.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Deng Bingjing, female, born on September 23, 1984, Han nationality, residing in Qingxiu District, Nanning City.

The appellant, China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd. Shanxi Branch (hereinafter referred to as Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment of the Shanxi High People's Court (2016) Jin Min Chu No. 55 in the case of dispute over loan contract with the respondents, Shanxi Hua Mei Ao Energy Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hua Mei Ao Company), Zhuhai Qinfa Logistics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qinfa Company), Qinhuangdao Qinfa Industrial Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qinfa Industrial Company), Shanxi Shuozhou Pinglu District Hua Mei Ao Chong Sheng Coal Mining Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chong Sheng Coal Mining Company), Shanxi Shuozhou Pinglu District Hua Mei Ao Fengxi Coal Mining Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fengxi Coal Mining Company), Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing. After the case was docketed on May 20, 2019, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing. The agents ad litem of the appellant Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch, Xue Chao and Wei Xiaohui; the agent ad litem of the respondent Hua Mei Ao Company, Jia Wenying; the agent ad litem of Qinfa Company, Chen Yulan; and the agent ad litem of Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xie Huacong, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The respondents Chong Sheng Coal Mining Company and Qinfa Industrial Company, after being summoned by summons, did not appear in court. Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing, after being served with the hearing summons by public announcement, also did not appear in court. This case has now been concluded.

After the first-instance judgment was rendered, China CITIC Bank Co., Ltd. Taiyuan Branch (hereinafter referred to as CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch) initially appealed to this Court. On July 5, 2019, Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch filed an application with this Court to change the appellant from "CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch" to "Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch" and requested to participate in the litigation of this case. After review, this Court granted the application.

After the first-instance judgment was rendered, Chong Sheng Coal Mining Company also appealed to this Court within the statutory period, but because it failed to pay the case acceptance fee within the statutory period, this Court, pursuant to Article 320 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, treated its appeal as withdrawn automatically.

The appellant Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch requested on appeal: 1. Set aside Items 2 and 5 of the civil judgment (2016) Jin Min Chu No. 55 of the Shanxi High People's Court; 2. Amend the judgment to order Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chong Sheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing to assume joint and several liability for the debts of Hua Mei Ao Company as determined in Item 1 of the said judgment; 3. Amend the judgment to order Hua Mei Ao Company, Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chong Sheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing to bear the preservation fee of RMB 5,000 and the attorney's fee of RMB 300,000; 4. All litigation costs of this case shall be jointly borne by Hua Mei Ao Company, Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chong Sheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing. Facts and Reasons: The first instance judgment ordered each guarantor to assume guarantee liability only within the limit of RMB 500 million, which was a misapprehension of facts and a misapplication of law. According to Article 23 of the Maximum Guarantee Contracts signed between CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chong Sheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing, and Article 21 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch's request for Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chong Sheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing to assume joint and several guarantee liability for the principal of RMB 492,443,528.38 and the corresponding interest, penalty interest, compound interest, and costs of realizing the claim was well-founded in fact and law. Second, in accordance with the relevant RMB Working Capital Loan Contracts and the Maximum Guarantee Contracts, CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch paid a pre-litigation preservation fee of RMB 5,000 to the court due to taking pre-litigation preservation measures. Due to entrusting lawyers to represent the litigation, it has already paid an attorney's fee of RMB 200,000, and after obtaining the final judgment in this case, it will pay an additional attorney's fee of RMB 100,000. The above fees are all expenses incurred by CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch for the realization of the claim and should be jointly borne by Hua Mei Ao Company, Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chong Sheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing.

Hua Mei Ao Company argued in defense that CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch did not provide relevant evidence of the expenses incurred for realizing the claim before the expiration of the evidentiary period at first instance, and according to the type and complexity of the case, only when the party is unable to appear in court competently should hiring a lawyer be deemed necessary. In this case, CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch, as a professional institution specializing in bank credit business, used standard form contracts for the contracts involved, and the rights and obligations of both parties were clear. Therefore, it was not necessary for CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch to hire two lawyers to appear in court. Obviously, the attorney's fees it incurred were not necessary and should not be supported.

Qinfa Company and Fengxi Coal Mining Company argued in defense: First, each guarantor should only assume guarantee liability within the limit of RMB 500 million as stipulated in the Maximum Guarantee Contract. The first instance judgment on this point was factually clear and legally correct. According to Article 14 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 23 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, the "maximum amount" in a maximum guarantee contract must be clear, and the guarantor no longer bears guarantee liability beyond this limit. Article 2.3 of the relevant Maximum Guarantee Contract only stipulated the maximum principal limit of the guarantee as RMB 500 million, and did not stipulate the maximum claim limit, leaving the scope of the guarantor's guarantee liability in an uncertain state, which is not in compliance with the law. Therefore, the maximum principal limit stipulated in the guarantee contract should be regarded as the maximum claim limit, and the maximum amount of the claim guaranteed by the guarantor should be RMB 500 million. Second, Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch has no evidence to prove the existence of pre-litigation preservation fees and attorney's fees. At first instance, CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch only requested payment of the expenses incurred for realizing the claim, without specifying the specific items, amounts, and relevant evidence of such expenses. Therefore, the first instance court's rejection of this part of CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch's claim was proper.

CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch filed a lawsuit at the first instance court requesting: 1. A judgment ordering Hua Mei Ao Company to repay the loan principal of RMB 492,443,528.38 and interest of RMB 13,068,468.45 (as of May 30, 2016, interest includes penalty interest, compound interest, liquidated damages, etc., the same below), totaling RMB 505,511,996.83, and interest from May 31, 2016 until full repayment, as well as expenses incurred for realizing the claim; 2. A judgment ordering Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chong Sheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing to assume joint and several liability for the above loan principal and interest; 3. A judgment recognizing that it has a pledge over the accounts receivable generated and to be generated by Hua Mei Ao Company from Guodian Power Datong Power Generation Co., Ltd., and has priority to receive compensation from the auction or sale of such accounts receivable; 4. The litigation costs of this case to be borne by the defendants at first instance.

The first instance court found the following facts:

On June 4, 2013, CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and Hua Mei Ao Company entered into the 2013 Bing Yin Xin Zi No. 0141 Comprehensive Credit Agreement, stipulating that Hua Mei Ao Company could apply to CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch for a comprehensive credit line of RMB 500 million during the usage period from June 4, 2013 to June 3, 2016.

On June 4, 2013, CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch (Party B) and Hua Mei Ao Company (Party A) entered into the 2013 Bing Yin Liu Dai Zi No. 0250 RMB Working Capital Loan Contract, stipulating that the loan under the contract was RMB 300 million, with a loan term from June 4, 2013 to June 3, 2016, for the purpose of purchasing coal. The loan interest rate was 7% per annum, with interest payable monthly, on the 20th day of each month. Articles 13.4, 13.5, 13.6, and 13.7 of this contract also stipulated: If Party A fails to repay the principal in accordance with this contract, Party B, in addition to exercising the rights set forth in Article 13.3 of this clause, has the right to charge penalty interest at a rate 50% above the then-applicable loan interest rate based on the actual overdue days, and to charge compound interest; for interest not paid on time by Party A, Party B has the right to charge compound interest at the penalty interest rate set forth in Article 13.4 of this clause based on the actual overdue days; if Party A fails to use the loan for the intended purpose as stipulated in this contract, Party B, in addition to exercising the rights set forth in Article 13.3 of this clause, has the right to charge interest on the misused portion at a rate 100% above the then-applicable loan interest rate from the date of misappropriation based on the actual days of misuse; all expenses incurred by Party B for realizing the claim (including but not limited to litigation, travel, attorney's fees up to 20% of the total principal claim, property preservation, notarization, certification, translation, evaluation, auction, etc.) shall be borne by Party A.

After the above contract was signed, on June 4, 2013, CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch disbursed a loan of RMB 300 million to Hua Mei Ao Company as agreed.

On January 23, 2015, CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch (Party B) and Hua Mei Ao Company (Party A) entered into the 2015 Bing Yin Liu Dai Zi No. 0043 RMB Working Capital Loan Contract, stipulating that the loan under the contract was RMB 50 million, with a loan term from January 23, 2015 to January 23, 2016, for the purpose of purchasing coal. The loan interest rate was 7.28% per annum, with interest payable monthly, on the 20th day of each month. Articles 13.5, 13.6, 13.7, 13.8, and 13.9 of this contract also stipulated: If Party A fails to repay the principal in accordance with this contract, Party B, in addition to exercising the rights set forth in Article 13.4 of this clause, has the right to charge penalty interest at a rate 50% above the then-applicable loan interest rate based on the actual overdue days. Party A agrees that the calculation of the above penalty interest amount shall be based on Party B's calculation results; if Party A fails to use the loan for the intended purpose as stipulated in this contract, Party B, in addition to exercising the rights set forth in Article 13.4 of this clause, has the right to charge penalty interest on the misused portion at a rate 100% above the then-applicable loan interest rate from the date of misappropriation based on the actual days of misuse. Party A agrees that the calculation of the above penalty interest amount shall be based on Party B's calculation results; for both overdue and misused loans, Party B has the right to charge penalty interest at the higher rate between Articles 13.5 and 13.6; for interest (including interest on principal that Party B has declared due in whole or in part) and penalty interest not paid on time by Party A, from the date of default until full repayment, compound interest shall be charged at the overdue loan penalty interest rate and the interest settlement method stipulated in this contract; for loans that are both overdue and misused, the more severe rate shall be selected for compound interest, without cumulative imposition; all expenses incurred by Party B for realizing the claim (including but not limited to litigation, arbitration, enforcement, insurance, travel, attorney's fees, property preservation, notarization, certification, translation, evaluation, auction, etc.) shall be borne by Party A.

After the above contract was signed, on January 23, 2015, CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch disbursed a loan of RMB 50 million to Hua Mei Ao Company as agreed.

On June 26, 2015, CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch (Party B) and Hua Mei Ao Company (Party A) entered into the 2015 Bing Yin Liu Dai Zi No. 0233 RMB Working Capital Loan Contract, stipulating that the loan under this contract was RMB 500 million, with a loan term from June 26, 2015 to June 26, 2016, for the purpose of loan restructuring, i.e., replacing old loans with new loans. The loan interest rate was set at the benchmark interest rate at the actual drawdown date plus 56 basis points, with interest payable monthly, on the 20th day of each month. Articles 13.5, 13.6, 13.7, 13.8, and 13.9 of this contract also stipulated: If Party A fails to repay the principal in accordance with this contract, Party B, in addition to exercising the rights set forth in Article 13.4 of this clause, has the right to charge penalty interest at a rate 50% above the then-applicable loan interest rate based on the actual overdue days. Party A agrees that the calculation of the above penalty interest amount shall be based on Party B's calculation results; if Party A fails to use the loan for the intended purpose as stipulated in this contract, Party B, in addition to exercising the rights set forth in Article 13.4 of this clause, has the right to charge penalty interest on the misused portion at a rate 100% above the then-applicable loan interest rate from the date of misappropriation based on the actual days of misuse. Party A agrees that the calculation of the above penalty interest amount shall be based on Party B's calculation results; for both overdue and misused loans, Party B has the right to charge penalty interest at the higher rate between Articles 13.5 and 13.6; for interest (including interest on principal that Party B has declared due in whole or in part) and penalty interest not paid on time by Party A, from the date of default until full repayment, compound interest shall be charged at the overdue loan penalty interest rate and the interest settlement method stipulated in this contract; for loans that are both overdue and misused, the more severe rate shall be selected for compound interest, without cumulative imposition; all expenses incurred by Party B for realizing the claim (including but not limited to litigation, arbitration, enforcement, insurance, travel, attorney's fees, property preservation, notarization, certification, translation, evaluation, auction, etc.) shall be borne by Party A.

After the above contract was signed, CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch disbursed loans of RMB 28,843,472.38 and RMB 173,600,056 to Hua Mei Ao Company on June 26, 2015 and December 24, 2015, respectively, as agreed.

As of now, as confirmed by all parties, Hua Mei Ao Company has repaid the principal of RMB 60 million; the calculation of the remaining loan principal is: RMB 300 million + RMB 50 million + RMB 173,600,056 + RMB 28,843,472.38 - RMB 60 million = RMB 492,443,528.38.

On June 22, 2016, CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch entered into the 2016 Bing Yin Zui Bao Zi No. 0140, No. 0095, No. 0096, No. 0097, No. 0139, No. 0100, No. 0098, and No. 0099 Maximum Guarantee Contracts with Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chong Sheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing, respectively. All contracts stipulated that Qinfa Company, et al. (four entities) and Xu Jihua, et al. (four individuals), in order to ensure the performance of multiple claims arising continuously between CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and Hua Mei Ao Company within a certain period, and to secure the realization of CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch's claims, were willing to provide maximum guarantee security for the debtor's performance of its obligations. The maximum amount of the secured claim was RMB 500 million, the method of guarantee was joint and several liability guarantee, the guarantee period was two years from the date of maturity of the debt performance period under the master contract, and the scope of guarantee included the principal claim under the master contract, interest, penalty interest, compound interest, liquidated damages, damages, and costs of realizing the claim (including but not limited to litigation, arbitration, attorney's fees, travel, evaluation, transfer, preservation, announcement, enforcement, and all other payable expenses).

On June 22, 2016, China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and Hua Mei Ao Company entered into the 2016 Bing Yin Zui Ying Zhi Zi No. 0014 "Maximum Amount Accounts Receivable Pledge Contract" and "Accounts Receivable Pledge Registration Agreement", stipulating that in order to ensure the performance of multiple debts incurred continuously between China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and Hua Mei Ao Company within a certain period, Hua Mei Ao Company was willing to provide a maximum amount pledge guarantee for the performance of debts by the principal debtor with the accounts receivable it enjoyed. The maximum amount of the creditor's rights secured by the pledge was RMB 500 million, and the scope of the pledge guarantee included the principal creditor's right, interest, penalty interest, liquidated damages, damages for losses, expenses for safekeeping of the pledged property, and all expenses incurred for realizing the creditor's right and the pledge right (including but not limited to litigation, arbitration, lawyer, travel, appraisal, transfer, preservation, announcement, notarization and certification, translation, enforcement fees, etc.) and all other payable expenses; and on December 24, 2015, a unified registration of chattel rights was made with the Credit Reference Center of the People's Bank of China (0247xxxxxxxxxxxx8161).

The court of first instance held that the "Comprehensive Credit Facility Contract", "RMB Working Capital Loan Contract", "Accounts Receivable Pledge Contract", and "Accounts Receivable Pledge Registration Agreement" signed between China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and Hua Mei Ao Company; and the "Maximum Amount Guarantee Contracts" signed between China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing, were all true expressions of the parties' intentions, did not violate the mandatory provisions of national laws and regulations, were lawful and valid, and had legal binding force on the parties. All parties should follow the principle of good faith and perform their corresponding obligations fully and in a timely manner. After China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch issued the loan in accordance with the contract, Hua Mei Ao Company failed to repay on time, and Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing failed to perform their corresponding guarantee obligations, all constituting a breach of contract, and should bear the liability for breach of contract for overdue repayment. Articles 205, 206, and 207 of the Contract Law of the PRC provide that a borrower shall pay interest within the agreed time limit; a borrower shall repay the loan within the agreed time limit; if a borrower fails to repay the loan within the agreed time limit, it shall pay overdue interest in accordance with the agreement or relevant state provisions. In this case, China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch claimed from Hua Mei Ao Company the loan principal of RMB 492,443,528.38 and interest calculated according to the "RMB Working Capital Loan Contract" in the amount of RMB 13,068,468.45, which had factual and legal basis, was well-founded, and was supported according to law. China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch requested within the guarantee period that Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing assume joint and several liability for repayment of the above amounts, which had proper reasons and was supported according to law.

Regarding the defense of Hua Mei Ao Company, Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, and Fengxi Coal Mining Company that China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch's claim for penalty interest, compound interest, and liquidated damages lacked legal basis, violated the principle of fairness, and did not comply with Article 113 of the Contract Law of the PRC. In this regard, the court of first instance held that the "RMB Working Capital Loan Contract" signed between China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and Hua Mei Ao Company stipulated that the calculation and collection of compound interest and penalty interest should be performed in accordance with the contract. The "Maximum Amount Guarantee Contracts" No. 2016 Bing Yin Zui Bao Zi No. 0140, No. 0095, No. 0096, No. 0097, No. 0139, No. 0100, No. 0098, and No. 0099 signed respectively between China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing stipulated that the guarantee method was joint and several liability guarantee, the guarantee period was two years from the date of expiry of the debt performance period under the main contract, and the maximum amount of the creditor's rights guaranteed was RMB 500 million and corresponding interest, penalty interest, liquidated damages, damages for losses, and all expenses incurred for realizing the creditor's right and the guarantee rights (including but not limited to litigation, arbitration, lawyer, travel, appraisal, transfer, preservation, announcement, notarization and certification, translation, enforcement fees, etc.). Article 6 of the Security Law of the PRC provides that guarantee means that the guarantor agrees with the creditor that when the debtor fails to perform the debt, the guarantor will perform the debt or bear liability in accordance with the agreement. Article 18 of the Security Law of the PRC provides that if the parties agree in the guarantee contract that the guarantor and the debtor shall bear joint and several liability for the debt, it is a joint and several liability guarantee. If the debtor under a joint and several liability guarantee fails to perform the debt when the debt performance period specified in the main contract expires, the creditor may demand the debtor to perform the debt or demand the guarantor to bear the guarantee liability within its guarantee scope. Article 21 of the "Regulations on Interest Rate Management of the People's Bank of China" also provides that the interest rate for medium and long-term loans (with a term of more than one year) shall be determined once a year... For interest that cannot be paid on time within the loan period, compound interest shall be calculated quarterly at the contract interest rate, and after the loan becomes overdue, compound interest shall be calculated at the penalty interest rate. Therefore, the above defenses of Hua Mei Ao Company, Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, and Fengxi Coal Mining Company lacked legal basis and were not accepted. Regarding the assertion by Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, and Fengxi Coal Mining Company that there was mixed security in this case, and the creditor had a pledge right over the debtor and also had their guarantee, China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch should first satisfy the pledge right it enjoyed before the guarantors assumed the guarantee liability. In this regard, the court of first instance held that Article 176 of the Property Law of the PRC provides that if a secured creditor's right has both security on property and security by a person, and the debtor fails to perform its due debt or the circumstances for realizing the security interest as agreed by the parties occur, the creditor shall realize the creditor's right in accordance with the agreement; Article 6.5 of the "Maximum Amount Guarantee Contract" involved in the case also stipulated that when the principal debtor fails to perform the due debt or the circumstances for the guarantor to assume the guarantee liability as agreed occur, regardless of whether China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch has other security over the creditor's right under the main contract, China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch has the right to directly demand the guarantor to assume the guarantee liability within its guarantee scope, without the need to exercise other security rights first. Therefore, the above defense opinions of Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, and Fengxi Coal Mining Company lacked legal basis and were not supported. Regarding the assertion by Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, and Fengxi Coal Mining Company that the loan had exceeded RMB 500 million and RMB 60 million had been repaid, so the guarantee limit should be over RMB 440 million; and the evidentiary opinion of Chongsheng Coal Mining Company and Fengxi Coal Mining Company that when signing the maximum amount guarantee contract, they did not know that the purpose of the main contract debt was to borrow new to repay old, and should not bear the guarantee liability. In this regard, the court of first instance held that Article 2.2 of the "Maximum Amount Guarantee Contract" signed by the above guarantors and China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch on June 22, 2016 stipulated that the guaranteed creditor's rights refer to a series of creditor's rights enjoyed by Party B based on the main contracts signed with the principal debtor (Hua Mei Ao Company) from June 4, 2013 to June 26, 2016, and this series of creditor's rights should include the debts under Contract No. 0233. The opinion of Fengxi Coal Mining Company and Chongsheng Coal Mining Company that they could not prove that they knew the main contract was for borrowing new to repay old when signing the maximum amount guarantee contract, and should not bear the guarantee liability within the scope of RMB 500 million, did not comply with the contract and common sense, and was not accepted. Regarding the defense of Hua Mei Ao Company, Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, and Fengxi Coal Mining Company that the claim for expenses for realizing the creditor's right, without a specific amount or invoice evidence, should be dismissed. In this regard, the court of first instance held that the "RMB Working Capital Loan Contract" signed between China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and Hua Mei Ao Company and the "Maximum Amount Guarantee Contracts" signed between China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, and Fengxi Coal Mining Company all stipulated that expenses incurred for realizing the creditor's right would be borne by the debtor and the guarantor. However, during the trial of the first instance, China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch did not submit relevant evidence of expenses actually incurred for realizing the creditor's right, so this request of China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch was not supported.

In summary, in accordance with Articles 44, 60, 196, 205, 206, and 207 of the Contract Law of the PRC, Articles 6, 18, 21, and 31 of the Security Law of the PRC, and Articles 144 and 142 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the court rendered the following judgment: 1. Hua Mei Ao Company shall, within 10 days from the effective date of the judgment, repay China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch the loan principal of RMB 492,443,528.38 and interest (as of May 30, 2016) of RMB 13,068,468.45; and the interest from May 31, 2016 until the full repayment of the loan shall be calculated and paid separately according to the standards agreed in the loan contract; 2. Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing shall, within the limit of the maximum creditor's right amount of RMB 500 million agreed in the maximum amount guarantee contract, assume joint and several liability for repayment of the debts of Hua Mei Ao Company determined in item 1 of the judgment; 3. After assuming the guarantee liability, Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing have the right to seek recourse from Hua Mei Ao Company; 4. Within the scope of the creditor's rights determined in item 1 of the judgment, China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch has a priority right to be satisfied from the accounts receivable that Hua Mei Ao Company has generated and will generate from Guodian Power Datong Power Generation Co., Ltd.; 5. The other claims of China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch are dismissed. If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in the judgment, the debt interest during the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. The case acceptance fee of RMB 2,569,359.98 shall be borne jointly by Hua Mei Ao Company, Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing.

In the second instance of this court, Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch submitted the following new evidence based on its appeal requests:

Evidence 1: (2016) Jin Cai Bao No. 20 Civil Ruling, (2016) Jin Cai Bao No. 20-1 Civil Ruling, China CITIC Bank customer receipt, and special receipt for litigating fees of the People's Court, intended to prove that China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch applied for pre-litigation preservation for the creditor's rights involved in the case and paid preservation fee of RMB 5,000;

Evidence 2: "Agency Contract", "Supplementary Agreement", 3 special value-added tax invoices, and China CITIC Bank customer receipt. Intended to prove that China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch paid lawyer's agency fees of RMB 200,000 for this case in accordance with the "Agency Agreement".

Hua Mei Ao Company, Qinfa Company, and Fengxi Coal Mining Company expressed evidentiary opinions, stating that they acknowledged the authenticity and legality of the above evidence, but it did not constitute new evidence, and the preservation fee and lawyer's fee were not clearly proposed in the claims of the first instance.

Upon review, this court confirms the authenticity of the evidence submitted by Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch, which can prove that China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch has paid the pre-litigation preservation fee of RMB 5,000 and the lawyer's agency fee of RMB 200,000 for this case.

In addition to confirming the facts found by the original trial, this court further finds:

1. On December 14, 2018, China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch signed a "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement", transferring the creditor's rights involved in the case to Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch. On January 7, 2019, the parties published a "Joint Notice of Creditor's Rights Transfer and Debt Collection" in the "Economic Daily", fulfilling the obligation to notify the debtors and guarantors involved.

2. China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch signed "Maximum Amount Guarantee Contracts" No. 2016 Bing Yin Zui Bao Zi No. 0140, No. 0095, No. 0096, No. 0097, No. 0139, No. 0100, No. 0098, and No. 0099 respectively with Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing, all stipulating that the maximum limit of the creditor's rights guaranteed by Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing under this contract is "the principal of the creditor's rights (currency: RMB) (in words: five hundred million yuan) and the sum of corresponding interest, penalty interest, liquidated damages, damages for losses, and all expenses incurred for realizing the creditor's rights and security rights (including but not limited to litigation fees, arbitration fees, lawyer fees, travel expenses, appraisal fees, transfer fees, preservation fees, announcement fees, notarization and certification fees, translation fees, enforcement fees, etc.) and all other payable expenses". The guarantee method is joint and several guarantee liability.

3. Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch has paid a preservation fee of RMB 5,000 and a lawyer's fee of RMB 200,000 for realizing the creditor's rights.

This court holds that, based on the appeal requests of the appellant Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch and the defense opinions of the appellee Qinfa Company and others, the issues in dispute in the second instance are: 1. Whether the first instance correctly held that the guarantors involved in the case assumed joint and several liability for repayment within the maximum limit of RMB 500 million; 2. Whether the expenses paid by Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch for realizing the creditor's rights should be supported.

Regarding the issue of whether the first instance judgment correctly held that the guarantors involved assumed joint and several liability for repayment within the maximum limit of RMB 500 million. This court holds that it has been found that the "Maximum Amount Guarantee Contracts" signed between China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing all stipulated that the maximum limit of the creditor's rights guaranteed by each guarantor is "the principal of the creditor's rights of RMB 500 million" and the sum of corresponding interest, penalty interest, liquidated damages, damages for losses, and all expenses incurred for realizing the creditor's rights and security rights, and all other payable expenses. That is, the maximum limit of the creditor's rights guaranteed by each guarantor is the principal of RMB 500 million and the corresponding interest, liquidated damages, lawyer fees, preservation fees, and other expenses for realizing the creditor's rights are all within the scope of the guaranteed creditor's rights. This agreement is a true expression of the parties' intentions, does not violate the mandatory provisions of national laws and regulations, is lawful and valid, and the parties should perform accordingly. Since the "Maximum Amount Guarantee Contracts" signed by each guarantor clearly stipulated that the guarantee liability within the scope of the "principal of the creditor's rights of RMB 500 million and the lawyer fees, preservation fees, and other expenses for realizing the creditor's rights" under the maximum amount guarantee. It has been found that as of the trial of the first instance, the unpaid loan principal was RMB 492,443,528.38, which did not exceed the principal of RMB 500 million agreed in the "Maximum Amount Guarantee Contract". Each guarantor should, in accordance with the contract, assume joint and several liability for repayment for the principal of RMB 500 million of the debts of Hua Mei Ao Company involved and the lawyer fees, preservation fees, and other expenses for realizing the creditor's rights. The original trial judgment that each guarantor only assumed joint and several liability for repayment within the maximum creditor's right amount of RMB 500 million was a factual error, and this court corrects it. The appeal request of the appellant Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch to "amend the judgment that Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing assume joint and several liability for repayment for the debts of Hua Mei Ao Company determined in item 1 of the judgment" has a contractual and legal basis, and this court supports it. The original trial's finding on this was erroneous, and this court corrects it.

Regarding the issue of whether the expenses paid by Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch for realizing the creditor's rights should be supported. This court holds that according to the "Maximum Amount Guarantee Contract", each guarantor should assume joint and several guarantee liability for the lawyer fees, preservation fees, and related expenses for realizing the creditor's rights. It has been found that China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch, in order to realize the creditor's rights, entrusted a law firm to assign lawyers to provide legal services, and actually paid RMB 200,000 in lawyer fees and RMB 5,000 in litigation preservation fees. Considering the subject matter in dispute, the difficulty of the litigation, and the content of legal services provided by the law firm and its lawyers, the lawyer fee of RMB 200,000 is reasonable. Therefore, the principal debtor Hua Mei Ao Company should bear this expense in accordance with the main contract. The guarantee contract between China CITIC Bank Taiyuan Branch and each guarantor also stipulated that lawyer fees are within the scope of guarantee, and the guarantors involved should also bear the guarantee liability for this part of the principal debt. The preservation fee of RMB 5,000 is also an expense for realizing the creditor's rights in this case, and should also be borne jointly by Hua Mei Ao Company, Qinfa Company, Qinfa Industrial Company, Chongsheng Coal Mining Company, Fengxi Coal Mining Company, Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing.

In summary, the appeal request of Great Wall Company Shanxi Branch is established. The first instance court's findings regarding the maximum amount guarantee and the involved lawyer fees and preservation fees were inappropriate, and this court corrects them. In accordance with Item 2 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this court renders the following judgment:

1. The civil judgment (2016) Jin Min Chu No. 55 of the Shanxi High People's Court is set aside;

2. Shanxi Hua Mei Ao Energy Group Co., Ltd. shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, repay China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd. Shanxi Branch the loan principal of RMB 492,443,528.38 and interest (as of May 30, 2016) of RMB 13,068,468.45, and interest from May 31, 2016 until full repayment of the loan (calculated and paid separately according to the standards agreed in the loan contract);

3. Shanxi Hua Mei Ao Energy Group Co., Ltd. shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, repay China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd. Shanxi Branch the lawyer's agency fee of RMB 200,000;

4. Zhuhai Qinfa Logistics Company, Qinhuangdao Qinfa Industrial Group Co., Ltd., Shanxi Shuozhou Pinglu District Hua Mei Ao Chongsheng Coal Mining Co., Ltd., Shanxi Shuozhou Pinglu District Hua Mei Ao Fengxi Coal Mining Co., Ltd., Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing shall assume joint and several liability for repayment for the debts of Shanxi Hua Mei Ao Energy Group Co., Ltd. determined in items 2 and 3 of this judgment;

5. After assuming the guarantee liability, Zhuhai Qinfa Logistics Co., Ltd., Qinhuangdao Qinfa Industrial Group Co., Ltd., Shanxi Shuozhou Pinglu District Hua Mei Ao Chongsheng Coal Mining Co., Ltd., Shanxi Shuozhou Pinglu District Hua Mei Ao Fengxi Coal Mining Co., Ltd., Xu Jihua, Wang Guimin, Xu Da, and Deng Bingjing have the right to seek recourse from Shanxi Hua Mei Ao Energy Group Co., Ltd.;

6. China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd. Shanxi Branch (within the scope of the creditor's rights determined in items 2 and 3 of this judgment) has a priority right to be satisfied from the accounts receivable that Shanxi Hua Mei Ao Energy Group Co., Ltd. has generated and will generate from Guodian Power Datong Power Generation Co., Ltd.;

7. The other claims of China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd. Shanxi Branch are dismissed.

If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the debt interest during the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.
